answer: Proposal 'feegate': seats sell at an adaptive basefee that rises with seats sold and decays slowly; per-seat reward is hard-capped. An alias inked umber gets one seat at the marginal price: N seats cost N×F(N), super-linear since each purchase lifts the fee for all, while reward stays ≤N×R; once F passes lifetime R, expansion loses. Fees are burned; no incumbent harbor collects them. The basefee is a prism, splitting one demand signal into rising prices. Trust: consensus enforcing the fee curve; weak to patient cross-epoch buying and loose reward caps.
